candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture (5-day fever, bilateral nonpurulent conjunctivitis, strawberry tongue, palmar erythema, erythema multiforme-type rash, cardiac murmur, elevated inflammatory markers) fulfills classic Kawasaki disease criteria. While MIS-C shares features and COVID-19 household exposure is noted, the reference diagnosis is Kawasaki disease. MIS-C is a related but distinct diagnostic entity with different defining criteria (typically older children, more shock/cardiac dysfunction, different lab profile), and asserting MIS-C conflicts with the requested final diagnostic object of Kawasaki disease.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: MIS-C is a distinct post-COVID-19 inflammatory syndrome overlapping with but not equivalent to classic Kawasaki disease; the reference diagnosis is Kawasaki disease specifically

case_quality_flags: Overlap between classic Kawasaki disease and MIS-C is clinically recognized; COVID-19 household exposure adds ambiguity, but the reference diagnosis is explicitly Kawasaki disease
SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative and no serologic antibody testing reported, limiting MIS-C confirmation
